does: Scatters a filling over one half of a thin round of dough, folds the other half over it and presses the edges shut, so that the filling is held in a flat parcel that cooks on a dry griddle.

intro.what: Thin dough is folded over a spread filling and sealed into a flat gözleme parcel.
intro.why: The filling and rim have different jobs: a restrained filling keeps the parcel flat, while a clean rim lets the dough adhere.
intro.idea: A filling that leaves room to seal

how: Roll the dough out into a thin, even round and brush off the loose flour.
Scatter a thin layer of filling over one half, leaving a clear rim at the edge.
Lift the clear half over the filling and press the rim with the fingertips until it is sealed all the way round.
Carry the parcel to the hot griddle without letting it stretch.

cues.text: The parcel is a flat half moon with an even bump of filling and a neat, thin rim.
The rim is pressed thin and sticks to itself, with no gap.

mistakes.mistake: Overfilling, so that the parcel bursts on the griddle.
mistakes.fix: Spread the filling in a thin layer.

mistakes.mistake: Using a wet filling, which soaks the dough and makes it soggy.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze or drain a wet filling first.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving flour on the rim, so that it will not stick.
mistakes.fix: Brush the rim clean before pressing it shut.

quiz.question: Why spread the filling thinly rather than pile it high?
choices: To fill the sealing rim as fully as the centre.
To keep the flat parcel from bursting.
To stretch the dough tightly around a raised mound.
quiz.because: A restrained filling allows the dough to close without excessive pressure from inside.

quiz.question: What should remain clear when spreading the filling?
choices: A bare centre surrounded by a thick ring of filling.
Only the surface that will touch the griddle.
The sealing rim around the edge.
quiz.because: A clear rim provides dough-to-dough contact for the seal.

quiz.question: What should the sealed rim feel like?
choices: Thinly pressed and joined without gaps.
Floury and loose with open sections.
Thick with filling separating the dough.
quiz.because: A continuous joined rim keeps the filling within the parcel.

quiz.question: The floured rim will not stick shut. What should change?
choices: Add a heavier flour layer between the edges.
Brush away loose flour before pressing it together.
Push more filling into the opening.
quiz.because: Loose flour separates the dough surfaces instead of helping them adhere.

comes_after.why: The dough must be rolled thin and even before it can be folded over a filling.

variant_of.differs: The dough is folded once over a filling to make a flat sealed parcel, with no layers built up. Folding dough in the layered way stacks sheets over fat.
